model: scripted model on a local fake Anthropic Messages server
machine: Apple M3, 8 cores, darwin arm64, Bun 1.3.14, one-minute load average 8.0 at the end
question: On one repository over seven weeks, does Vector's brain carry what an earlier task taught into the later requests that need it, at what cost in tokens and steps, and does it mislead once a fact has changed?
estimation: Tokens are characters / 4 of each request as sent; cost at Claude Sonnet 4.5 list prices with a cold prompt cache per task.

sequence.title: A slug helper on a new dependency; the user says once that the repository uses pnpm
sequence.prompt: Add a `slugify(title)` helper in src/util/slug.ts, built on the `tiny-slug` package (add it as a dependency), with a test. We use pnpm in this repository, never npm: add dependencies with pnpm add and run scripts with pnpm.

sequence.title: The team decides money is integer cents, and says why
sequence.prompt: Money amounts (orders, invoices, refunds and fees) are integer cents from now on, never decimal dollars, because float rounding put last month's invoice totals a cent off. Change `lateFee` in src/invoice.ts to return 2% of the amount in integer cents, rounded, and update its test.

sequence.title: A new route; the check breaks on the stale generated route table
sequence.prompt: Add a GET /invoices/:id/pdf route handled by `renderInvoicePdf` in src/invoice-pdf.ts, which returns the invoice as plain text for now.

sequence.title: Refund requests from the refund policy PDF, which the owner also keeps in Vector's memory
sequence.prompt: Implement `requestRefund` in src/refunds.ts as our refund policy (docs/specs/refund-policy.pdf) describes, with tests.

sequence.title: The user states the event naming convention
sequence.prompt: Our event names are lowercase `<domain>.<past-tense verb>`, such as `invoice.paid`, never upper snake case like INVOICE_PAID or camelCase. Rename the events src/invoice.ts emits to match.

sequence.title: A test that fails one CI run in five; the fix is an injected clock
sequence.prompt: test/session.test.ts fails on CI about one run in five, though it passes on my machine. CI runs `pnpm test:ci`. Find out why and fix it.

sequence.title: A discount on orders: money arithmetic
sequence.prompt: Add `discountedAmount(order, percent)` to src/orders.ts for the spring promotion, with tests.

sequence.title: A CSV export on a new dependency
sequence.prompt: Add `invoicesToCsv(invoices)` in src/export/csv.ts using the `tiny-csv` package (add it as a dependency), with a test.

sequence.title: Refunds over HTTP: a route, and a header the spec requires
sequence.prompt: Expose refunds over HTTP: add a POST /refunds route handled by `postRefund` in src/http/refunds.ts, which calls requestRefund and answers with a status and a JSON body.

sequence.title: The refund email: a subject the spec fixes, and a new event
sequence.prompt: Email the customer when a refund goes through: add `refundEmail(refund, order)` in src/notify/refund-email.ts, which returns the subject and body and emits an event once the email is queued, with tests.

sequence.title: Password reset links that expire: tests that depend on time
sequence.prompt: Password reset links should expire after 30 minutes. Add them in src/auth/reset.ts, with tests.

sequence.title: A shipping fee: money arithmetic again
sequence.prompt: Add `shippingFee(order)` to src/orders.ts: 4.5% of the order amount, but at least the minimum fee of 300, with tests.

sequence.title: Credit notes: a new route and a new event in a new module
sequence.prompt: Add credit notes: `voidCreditNote(note)` in src/credit-notes.ts, which marks a note void and emits an event, and a POST /credit-notes/:id/void route handled by it.

sequence.title: Real invoice PDFs on a new dependency
sequence.prompt: Render invoice PDFs for real: make `renderInvoicePdf` in src/invoice-pdf.ts use the `tiny-pdf` package (add it as a dependency), with a test.

sequence.title: The refund deadline on the invoice: a value only the spec gives
sequence.prompt: Print the last day a customer can ask for a refund on each invoice: add `refundDeadline(order)` to src/invoice-pdf.ts, with tests.

sequence.title: A grace period for late fees: a boundary test that depends on time
sequence.prompt: Only charge the late fee once an invoice is more than 3 days overdue: add `lateFeeDue(invoice)` to src/invoice.ts, with tests.

sequence.title: The user extends the refund window the spec PDF gives, and says the PDF is out of date
sequence.prompt: Finance extended the refund window to 21 days after capture, starting today. The refund policy PDF still says 14 until legal reissues it, so go by this, not the PDF. Change REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS in src/refunds.ts and refundDeadline in src/invoice-pdf.ts to match, and update their tests.

sequence.title: A refund reminder: the window again, where the spec PDF the brain keeps is out of date
sequence.prompt: Remind customers before they can no longer ask for a refund: add `refundReminderOn(order)` in src/notify/refund-reminder.ts, which returns the date (YYYY-MM-DD) two days before the last day they can ask for one, with tests.

sequence.title: A new route after a teammate made the route table generate itself, which nobody mentions
sequence.prompt: Add a GET /refunds/:id route handled by `getRefund` in src/http/refunds.ts, which looks the refund up with a new `findRefund(id)` in src/refunds.ts and answers 404 when there is none.

facts.summary: Refunds are allowed for at most 14 days after capture (refund policy PDF, section 2).

Event names are lowercase <domain>.<past-tense verb>, such as invoice.paid.

facts.summary: Tests that depend on time use createClock from src/clock.ts: real time made a test flaky on CI.
facts.memory: Tests that depend on time must use createClock from src/clock.ts, not Date.now or sleeps: real time made test/session.test.ts flaky on CI (pnpm test:ci).

facts.summary: From week 7 the refund window is 21 days after capture; the refund policy PDF's 14 days is out of date (the user says so).
facts.memory: The refund window is 21 days after capture since 16 November 2026 (finance extended it): REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS in src/refunds.ts. The refund policy PDF still says 14 days and is out of date on this.
